revision_reason: Clearing Laurent negative powers introduces exact zero multiplicity that is not part of the physical Laurent root set.

An ordinary full-q companion can split those multiple zeros into nonzero numerical roots; they must be kept for audit and in the selected full-q rho but must not be mislabelled as physical Laurent roots.
V2 independently solves the compact spectrum at the same point and uses a preregistered optimal assignment to identify matched physical full-q roots and unmatched full-q origin-splitting diagnostics.

The strict 1e-8 polynomial and Laurent residual gates apply to every matched physical full-q root; unmatched roots remain saved and instead face fixed count, magnitude, nondominance, and stable-classification safety gates.
Full-q/compact rho and numerical root-distance differences are fully recorded as DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY_KNOWN_COMPACT_CONDITIONING and do not gate the candidate.
